newsitem.title: FRENCH GUIANA: Ariane rocket launches U.S., Argentine satellites.
newsitem.headline: Ariane rocket launches U.S., Argentine satellites.

text.p: Western Europe's 93rd Ariane rocket blasted off from French Guiana on Thursday carrying satellites for the United States and Argentina.
The Ariane 44L rocket lifted-off at 7.04 p.m (2204 GMT) into a cloudy equatorial night sky with its heaviest payload, weighing over 10,800 pounds (4.9 tonnes).

Twenty minutes later space officials said the U.S. GE-2 satellite separated from the Ariane rocket. Four minutes later NAHUEL 1A Argentina's first telecommunications satellite was released into space.
Thursday's launch was the 22nd straight success of the Ariane-4 rocket series launched from the European Space Agency (ESA) launch centre in Kourou on the northeast coast of South America.
It was the sixth Ariane mission since the failure of the first experimental Ariane-5 rocket, 37 seconds after its maiden flight on June 4.
